purpose: Admit bounded derivations over the separately admitted CAPTURE_001 and CAPTURE_002 records without adding external observations, changing edge standing, selecting a preferred demonstration view, or authorizing external action.

lens_shift.surface_reading: Two captures returned the same per-edge result classes.
lens_shift.deeper_derivation_object: The derivation surface is the relation between two coordinate-bound graph states: what can be derived from repeated standing, repeated missingness, a second observation coordinate, and one separately labeled supplemental observation without interpolating continuity or inheriting authority.

rules: Derive only from objects already admitted before AG6.
Compare homologous edge classes only where CAPTURE_001 and CAPTURE_002 used the same frozen evaluation ruleset.
Do not interpolate relation standing across the unobserved interval between capture coordinates.
Treat CAPTURE_002 artifact identity as a carried-forward reference to the CAPTURE_001 admitted identity, not as a new byte reacquisition or rehash.
Repeated missingness in the capture record is not evidence that the external object or proposition is absent.
A supplemental observation introduced only at CAPTURE_002 remains separately labeled and is not retroactively imported into CAPTURE_001.
A derivation may describe deltas, invariances, and unresolved bridges but may not strengthen the standing of any underlying edge.
A derivation object is not a selected or privileged demonstration view.
A derived representation does not authorize external action.

derived_objects.statement: CAPTURE_002 carries forward the same filename, byte length, and SHA-256 identity tuple admitted for CAPTURE_001.
basis: CAPTURE_002 recomputation independently reproduced the carry-forward match

derived_objects.statement: Across the ten source surfaces made comparable by the CAPTURE_001-preserved field projection, CAPTURE_002 recorded ten matches and zero changed preserved-field projections.
All nine homologous edge classes have the same bounded result class at CAPTURE_001 and CAPTURE_002 under FORK-RRD-001-AG4-EVAL-v0.1.

Both capture records preserve the same two material missingness conditions relevant to evaluated edges: checksum assertion content was not captured and an attestation bundle/decoded predicate was not captured.
effects: ARTIFACT_TO_PUBLISHED_DIGEST remains INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE at both coordinates
attestation-dependent edge classes remain INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE at both coordinates

derived_objects.statement: CAPTURE_002 contains one separately labeled supplemental observation that CAPTURE_001 did not preserve: the repository latest-release endpoint reported v0.22.5.

The evidence record has greater temporal resolution after CAPTURE_002 because it contains a second independently bounded observation/evaluation coordinate and an additional separately labeled supplemental surface, while preserving CAPTURE_001 unchanged.

The CAPTURE_002 record graph is not identical to the CAPTURE_001 record graph because it is bound to a different observation coordinate and includes a separately labeled supplemental observation, even though the primary preserved-field projections and per-edge result classes are stable.
No admitted object supplies a bridge establishing that any external relation continuously persisted throughout the interval between CAPTURE_001 and CAPTURE_002.

The later v0.22.5 release observation does not establish either supersession or non-supersession of the bounded relations around v0.22.1; the corresponding edge remains INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE at CAPTURE_002.

No homologous edge class acquired a stronger result category between the two admitted coordinates; the derivation layer therefore adds temporal and comparative resolution without strengthening underlying edge standing.
